beats.note: CrowdStrike's own summary says a third-party review confirmed the bug is not exploitable by a threat actor. It was a data mismatch inside its own software.

beats.text: The code read past the end of a list.
beats.note: The full report, as TechTarget quotes it, describes an out-of-bounds memory read beyond the end of the input data array. On Windows, that meant a system crash.

beats.context: What the code supplied. The template type had defined 21 input fields. One too few, and 8 million machines or more went into reboot loops.

beats.note: The report says the mismatch evaded multiple layers of build validation and testing, partly because the tests used wildcard matching criteria.
That is when the Channel File 291 update was delivered to certain Windows hosts. By 29 July, about 99 per cent of Windows sensors were back online.

beats.text: Updates now go out in stages.
beats.note: New content must pass successive deployment rings before production, with canary testing, and the code now checks the number of input fields.

beats.text: The sensor expected 20 values. Someone had defined 21.
